name: Cinderblock Collective
description: A Tier 1 production collective operating out of decommissioned water treatment infrastructure beneath the Shelf's Ward Fourteen, Cinderblock Collective produces raw neural-feed dramas and documentary hybrids using salvaged BCI rigs and unlicensed immersion hardware. Their work circulates exclusively through pirate mesh networks and physical memory chips, bypassing Vantablack licensing entirely. Known for unflinching portrayals of corponation debt cycles and forced augmentation, their productions have been formally banned by both Axiom and HelixCorp territories.
cultural_impact: Cinderblock Collective established the aesthetic template for Shelf guerrilla neural-feed — low-resolution sensory halos, ambient industrial sound design, and deliberately incomplete narrative structures that became widely imitated across underground production circuits.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 journalist receives an anonymous memory chip containing an unfinished Cinderblock production that appears to document a real, ongoing corponation crime rather than fiction.
A Vantablack acquisitions operative is sent to locate and either recruit or neutralize Cinderblock's lead producer before a politically sensitive neural-feed drops on the pirate mesh.
A character discovers their own likeness — face, voice, neural signature — used without consent in a Cinderblock production, and must decide whether to expose the collective or protect it.
